questions.q: What tool and pattern are change approval workflows typically built with?
options: A legacy workflow editor exclusive to change_request, unrelated to any other process
Flow Designer, using the same multi-stage approval pattern taught in Catalog Automation
A hardcoded script with no configurable approval stages at all
Email rules with no record of approval anywhere in the platform
questions.explain: Change approval reuses the exact Flow Designer multi-stage approval pattern from Catalog Automation, just triggered on change_request instead of a catalog request.

questions.q: In the common two-stage Normal change pattern, which approval stage runs for every Normal change regardless of risk?
options: CAB approval only
Manager approval
Neither stage runs automatically
Emergency approver sign-off
questions.explain: Manager approval runs for every Normal change; CAB approval is added conditionally based on the risk value.

questions.q: What decides whether CAB approval gets added as a second stage after manager approval?
options: A flow condition checking change_request.risk — Medium or High continues into CAB approval, Low skips to Scheduled
Whichever approver happens to be online at the time
A random selection built into the flow
The requester manually choosing whether to add CAB approval
questions.explain: The branching condition evaluates the calculated risk field right after manager approval resolves, with no manual judgment involved.

questions.q: Why does a later stage in the chain (CAB approval) not start until the earlier stage (manager approval) is actually approved?
options: Because both stages always run in parallel with no dependency
Because that's the defining trait of a sequential multi-stage approval chain, the same pattern taught in Catalog Automation
Because CAB approval is unrelated to manager approval entirely
Because Flow Designer cannot support more than one approval action per flow
questions.explain: Sequential chaining means Stage 2 only begins once Stage 1's approval record is actually resolved as approved.

questions.q: What should a well-implemented approval flow do if a manager or CAB rejects a change at any stage?
options: Silently leave the change sitting unapproved with no defined next step
Automatically delete the change record
Route the record back for rework or mark it rejected outright, giving the requester a clear outcome
Escalate directly to an Emergency approval path
questions.explain: A real implementation always defines a clear outcome on rejection rather than letting the record stall indefinitely.
